brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CET on 26 October; new research covers 05:10 CET to 17:10 CET on 26 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Russian Bombs and Drones Kill Three Civilians in Eastern Ukraine on Monday
items.lede: Children were among the wounded in Yasnohirka and Pavlohrad, and Sloviansk rescuers pulled a homeowner's body from a destroyed house.

sections.text: Russian aircraft dropped four guided bombs on homes and shops in the centre of Yasnohirka near Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk region, on 26 October, killing one person and wounding 10, including a 13-year-old girl, officials said [1][2]. In nearby Sloviansk an airstrike destroyed a private house and rescuers recovered the owner's body [1]. A Russian drone strike on Pavlohrad, in Dnipropetrovsk region, killed one person and injured seven, among them two 10-year-old girls, and damaged apartment buildings and a shop [1][3]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the casualty figures come from Ukrainian officials relayed by Ukrainian outlets, without independent confirmation; the Sloviansk death rests on one outlet.

items.title: Third Child Dies After a Russian Drone Hit a Park in Ukraine's Nova Vodolaha
items.lede: The boy's younger sister died at the scene a week ago, and Ukrainian officials now count three children among the dead.

sections.text: A 12-year-old boy, Artem Koval, died in a Kyiv hospital from injuries suffered in the Russian drone strike on Yuvileinyi Park in Nova Vodolaha, in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, on 19 October, community head Oleksandr Yesin said on Facebook [4]. His eight-year-old sister Arina was killed at the scene, and Ukrinform said the number of children killed has risen to three [4]. Regional head Oleh Syniehubov had put the toll a week ago at five dead, including two children, and 15 injured, seven of them children [5]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the boy died, because the local head reported it on record; the overall toll of the 19 October strike rests on Ukrainian officials.

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Claims a Strike on a Missile-Battery Plant in Yelets
items.lede: Kyiv says the plant is Russia's sole maker of batteries for glide-bomb guidance kits, so the hit targets supplies behind daily bombing of Ukrainian towns.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said on Monday that its forces struck the battery workshop of the Energia plant in Yelets, in Russia's Lipetsk region, on 25 October and overnight into 26 October, and that a fire broke out on the site [6][7]. It described Energia as the only maker of batteries for Russian glide-bomb guidance modules and a supplier of batteries for Iskander-M missiles and sea-launched cruise missiles [6][7]. The same statement gave damage results for earlier strikes on the Proton-Elektrotex plant in Oryol and the Tolyattikauchuk plant in Samara region [7]. No Russian official account of damage at the plant was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the strike and its effects rest on a Ukrainian military claim relayed by two Ukrainian outlets, without independent confirmation of damage.

items.title: Drone Debris Hits a Passenger Train as Ukraine Targets Russia's Voronezh
items.lede: Two men died and 17 were hurt, most aboard the Anapa–Moscow train, while a Ukrainian drone maker said it struck a synthetic-rubber plant.

sections.text: Voronezh Governor Alexander Gusev said 113 drones were downed over Russia's Voronezh region overnight into 26 October, more than 70 of them over the city, and that falling debris hit a train in a left-bank suburb, killing two men and injuring 17, including a child [8]. Russian Railways said a carriage of the Anapa–Moscow train No. 11 was damaged at Somovo station and traffic on the section was halted after the overhead line lost power [8][9]. Gusev confirmed fires at several industrial sites without naming them; Ukrainian drone maker Fire Point said its FP-1 drones hit the Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic-rubber plant [8][9]. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 290 drones over 16 regions overnight [9]. No Ukrainian General Staff claim for Voronezh was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that a large attack hit Voronezh and that the train was damaged, because Russian officials and two outlets agree. Casualty figures rest on the governor alone, and the target claim on a Ukrainian company.

items.title: Kremlin Says Renewed Talks With Ukraine Will Not Pause Russia's Strikes
items.lede: Moscow's spokesman left room for territorial compromises and local humanitarian truces like Oleshky, but ruled out any halt to fighting before a deal.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on 26 October that the decision to resume trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US does not imply any restrictions on combat operations, and that Russian forces continue massive strikes on Ukraine's military-industrial targets [10][11]. He said territorial compromises could become part of the talks but that Moscow did not want to discuss details publicly [10][12]. Asked about local truces, he said 'for humanitarian purposes, absolutely,' citing the Oleshky arrangement brokered with US First Lady Melania Trump [10][11]. Kyiv Post reported the Oleshky truce is due to take effect on 29 October, according to the White House [11]. Kommersant said the Kremlin had indicated the talks could take place in Abu Dhabi, in the UAE, around 10 November [12].
Confidence is high on what Peskov said, because three outlets from different countries report the briefing consistently. Dates and venue for the talks are not formally announced.

items.title: Russia Hits 15 Sites in Ukraine With 140 Drones and Four Missiles Overnight
items.lede: Air defences stopped 112 drones and three guided missiles, but at least four people were wounded in Zaporizhzhia and the raid ran past dawn.

sections.text: Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov reported a jet-drone hit in the city's Kholodnohirskyi district at 03:28 Kyiv time (02:28 CET) [13]. The Air Force warned of ballistic missiles at 03:33 Kyiv time, and media reported explosions in Kropyvnytskyi after missiles were tracked toward the city [13]. A strike on Zaporizhzhia damaged private houses, cars, and a commercial building, started a fire, and injured at least two people [13]. Ukraine's Air Force said that from 18:00 Kyiv time on 25 October (17:00 CET) Russia launched one Kh-31P anti-radiation missile, three Kh-59/69 guided missiles, and 140 attack drones, 70 of them jet-powered [14][1]. As of 08:00 Kyiv time, air defences had downed or suppressed the three Kh-59/69 missiles and 112 drones, with hits at 15 locations and debris at four more, and the attack was continuing [14]. The State Emergency Service later put the Zaporizhzhia wounded at four, and guided bombs hit two districts of Izium, where three people needed medical help [1].
Confidence is high on the Air Force figures, which two outlets report identically from the official statement. Damage details rest on Ukrainian officials relayed by Ukrainian media.

items.title: Zelensky Offers to Spare Russian Refineries if Moscow Stops Hitting Ukraine's Grid
items.lede: Kyiv also said army limits and neutrality are off the table at the November talks, while energy, Black Sea grain, and prisoners are open.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the TSN programme on 25 October that Ukraine would stop striking Russia's oil and diesel refining infrastructure if Russia stopped striking Ukraine's power grid, calling it a fair 'energy ceasefire' he had proposed to partners [15][16]. He said a trilateral meeting with US and Russian negotiating teams would take place in November, and that territory could only be discussed by leaders [17][16]. He listed energy, grain shipments in the Black Sea, and prisoner exchanges as the specifics he wanted on the table [17]. Zelensky said limits on Ukraine's army and neutrality were not up for discussion and that he would like to keep an 800,000-strong force [17][16]. He also said US warnings of imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes had been fully restored [16]. No Kremlin reply to the energy offer was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Zelensky made these remarks, because three outlets report the interview consistently. The November date rests on statements by the two sides, not on an announced schedule.

items.title: Russia's Belgorod Counts Three Dead and 30 Damaged Blocks After a Ukrainian Drone Swarm
items.lede: Russian officials later raised the city's death toll by one and reported another death in a separate daytime strike, while Kyiv made no claim.

sections.text: A large swarm of Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian city of Belgorod, near Ukraine's border, overnight into 25 October, and the regional headquarters confirmed a 'massive UAV attack' [18]. Russian authorities said on Sunday that two men were killed and 13 people injured in the city, AFP reported [19]. Mayor Valentin Demidov posted images of burning apartment blocks and cars and said homes and some social and commercial facilities were badly damaged [19]. The monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said the main target was the MegaGRINN shopping complex, the city's largest [18][20]. Acting Governor Aleksandr Shuvayev counted 154 attacks across the region in 24 hours, with two more men killed in the Shebekino and Graivoron districts [19]. On Sunday local authorities put the overnight toll in the city at three dead and 13 injured, said a separate drone strike later in the day killed another person, and Shuvayev said 30 apartment buildings were damaged, the Guardian reported [16]. No Ukrainian military claim for Belgorod city was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the toll, because Russian officials, a party to the war, are the only basis and counts differ between reports. Confidence on the target is low, because it rests on a monitoring channel.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Russia Claims Drone Strikes on Two Cargo Ships Bound for Ukraine's Ports
items.lede: Moscow added a second vessel heading for Odesa to its claims, but named neither ship and gave no damage details, and Reuters could not verify either.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones struck a cargo ship heading for Ukraine's Black Sea port of Chornomorsk overnight into 25 October, claiming the vessel was supplying Ukraine's armed forces, Reuters reported via Digi24 [1]. The ministry gave no name for the ship and no details of damage [1]. It also claimed strikes on three logistics sites in Kharkiv that it said stored dual-use goods [1]. Reuters said it could not verify the claims [1]. Later on Sunday the ministry said its drones had also struck a second cargo vessel en route to the port of Odesa during the day, again saying the ships supplied Ukraine's army; Reuters could not confirm it, the Guardian reported [2]. No Ukrainian confirmation of a ship being hit was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low on the strike itself, because it rests on Russia's Defence Ministry, a party to the war, relayed by one outlet and not independently verified.

items.title: French Navy Patrol Plane Flies From Romania to Guard Black Sea Shipping
items.lede: Paris says the NATO-tasked Atlantique 2 helped rescue crews from attacked merchant ships, while a US P-8A Poseidon has also patrolled off Bulgaria.

sections.text: A French Navy Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft has been operating over the western Black Sea from Constanța, Romania, after a run of drone attacks on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria [3][4]. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said in Varna, Bulgaria, on 24 October that the NATO-tasked plane had been in the region for two weeks and had helped in rescues, noting three ships attacked, one of which sank within minutes about 100 kilometres from Varna [4][3]. Flight-tracking data cited by the Romanian outlet Curs de Guvernare put its arrival in Constanța on 18 October, Militarnyi reported on 25 October [3]. A US Navy P-8A Poseidon from Sigonella in Sicily also patrolled near Bulgaria's coast [3]. NATO agreed on 20 October to step up Black Sea surveillance [3][4].
Confidence is high on the deployment, because the French minister confirmed it on record and two outlets report it. The arrival date rests on flight-tracking data relayed by one outlet.

items.title: Poland Says It Knows Which GRU Unit Runs Russia's Hybrid Attacks in Europe
items.lede: Radosław Sikorski did not name the military intelligence unit or show evidence, but warned that Moscow is planning escalation beyond daily cyberattacks and sabotage.

sections.text: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told CNN's Fareed Zakaria in an interview published on 25 October that Russia is waging a hybrid war against Europe, citing attacks in Poland, the UK, and Germany, arson, and a failed attempt to derail a train [5][6]. 'We know which specific GRU unit is behind this, and we know they are planning escalation,' he said, according to PAP [5][6]. He said Poland faces daily cyberattacks on hospitals and the financial and energy systems, plus drone incursions, espionage, and mapping of critical maritime infrastructure [5]. Sikorski did not name the unit or describe the evidence or the planned escalation [6]. He said more aid to Ukraine was the best answer to Russian provocations [5]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Sikorski made the statement, because two outlets carry the same quote from PAP. Confidence is low on the attribution itself, because Warsaw has published no evidence.

items.title: Dutch Cabinet Plans to Cut 25,000 Central-Government Jobs by 2035
items.lede: Police and defence are spared, but strained agencies such as the tax office and immigration service are not, and the Open Government Act may also be reformed.

sections.text: The Netherlands' state secretary Van der Burg has put the first number on the cabinet's plan to shrink the central government: about 25,000 fewer civil servants, some 16 percent of roughly 160,000 full-time posts, by 2035, NOS reported [1]. Police and defence are exempt, but agencies already under strain, such as the benefits agency UWV, the immigration service IND, and the tax office, are not [1]. He said the cuts depend on simpler rules, standardised IT, and AI, and that choices about what government stops doing are still to be worked out [1]. The cabinet is also looking at scrapping some of its 28 advisory councils and about 150 advisory committees and at reforming the Open Government Act, which journalists use to obtain official information [1]. He aims to finish most plans within six months [1]. No breakdown by ministry was given.
Confidence is high on the figures and exemptions, because NOS reports them from the state secretary's letter to parliament; this rests on one outlet so far.

items.title: Thousands Rally in Prague Against Czech Plan to Scrap Public-Media Licence Fees
items.lede: Broadcaster employees plan an all-day strike on 3 Nov, and organisers called another rally on Letná Plain for 15 Nov after the overnight first-reading vote.

sections.text: Thousands of people filled Prague's Old Town Square in the Czech Republic on Sunday to protest a coalition bill replacing Czech Television and Czech Radio licence fees with state funding, ČTK reported [2][3]. The lower house passed the bill in first reading at 04:36 on Saturday; it would cut the broadcasters' funding by about CZK 1.4 billion and now goes to committee [2][3]. Mikuláš Minář, head of the organisers Milion chvilek pro demokracii, called on Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and coalition partners Tomio Okamura and Petr Macinka to withdraw it and join a public debate [2]. Critics warn that state funding could expose the broadcasters to political pressure [3]. ČTK judged the crowd markedly larger than at the group's 28 Sep protest [2]. On Monday, at a briefing before flying to Algeria, Babiš said the coalition would not withdraw the bill, though its form would still be discussed, and that he would propose voluntary licence-fee payments at second reading; he said he respected the public's and staff's right to protest [4].

Confidence is high on the protest, the vote, and the organisers' demands, because ČTK via Czech Television and Expats.cz report them; the funding cut and the strike plan rest on Expats.cz, and no crowd estimate was published.

items.title: Macron Says Saturday Is 'at Risk' and Moves French Marches Out of City Centres
items.lede: The president ruled out a state of emergency for now, as the prime minister met student influencers and ministers prepared to replace the Parcoursup university-entry platform.

sections.text: France's President Emmanuel Macron said in Marseille on Monday that next Saturday would be "at risk" and that protest routes would stay outside city centres, AFP reported [5]. He said order was being held "without a state of emergency" but called one not taboo if things worsened [5]. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met eight student influencers before student organisations, and the National Assembly will debate Parcoursup's future on Wednesday, a ministry source said [6]. Student union Unef called a reported 15,000 extra university places far short of its 250,000 demand [6]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Saturday evening that the marches had gone smoothly, while acknowledging a great many incidents of violence; on Sunday the interior ministry put arrests at 1,314, replacing his initial estimate of nearly a thousand, with 53 officers injured [7][8]. Nice prosecutor Damien Martinelli is investigating attacks on marchers; 11 of 59 detained may belong to the far right [9][10]. Dijon's prosecutor opened an armed-violence inquiry into far-right stone-throwing at marchers [11]. The Yellow Vests have called further protests for 31 Oct [8].

Confidence is high on Macron's remarks, the arrest figures, and the Nice and Dijon inquiries, which AFP, franceinfo, and prosecutors report on record; the Parcoursup measures rest on an influencer's account.

items.title: Milan Prosecutors Detain Alleged Mastermind of Italy's Movimento 17 Ottobre
items.lede: Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old researcher, faces suspected incitement with terrorist aims and organised protest violence under the new decree, and his wife is also under investigation.

sections.text: Italian police on Saturday night detained Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old Italian researcher considered the mastermind of the Movimento 17 ottobre linked to last weekend's clashes in central Milan, on the order of Milan prosecutors, ANSA reported [12]. He is suspected of incitement to commit crimes aggravated by terrorist aims and of organised violence at public demonstrations under Article 420 bis of the new decree [12]. His wife is under investigation without arrest for the same offences [12]. On Sunday ANSA reported that only Siher and his wife administered the movement's chats, which had about 100,000 followers on Telegram and almost 50,000 on Instagram [13]. On Sunday evening Milan prosecutors said Siher had created a state of intimidation among the population through the movement, an element they cite for the terrorism aggravating factor, ANSA reported [14]. On Monday Milan prosecutors asked for Siher to be held in prison, arguing that his command of digital tools meant he could "develop a revolutionary strategy" and citing risks of flight and of reoffending, ANSA reported [15].
Confidence is high on the detention and the charges, because ANSA reports the prosecutors' order; the chat and intimidation details rest on ANSA summaries only.

items.title: Storm Boelo Kills Two Men in Britain and Cuts Power to 90,000 Properties
items.lede: About 90,000 British properties were still without power on Monday, and the Met Office issued a fresh yellow wind warning for Monday night.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Two men were killed by falling trees in the UK on Sunday during Storm Boelo: a man in his 20s whose car was hit in Finchley, north London, at about 13:40 CET, and a 60-year-old near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, police said, the BBC reported [16]. More than 90,000 properties were without power at 20:00 CET, the Energy Networks Association said, and 838,700 lost power during Storms Austen and Boelo [16]. Gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, the BBC reported [16]. The Portuguese-flagged freighter UHL Freedom, which lost anchor grip north of Schiermonnikoog, sailed on under limited power from 18:35 CET, the Dutch coastguard said; NOS now reports three of its 25 crew injured, down from five [17][18]. On Monday about 90,000 properties were still without power, the Energy Networks Association said, and the Met Office issued a yellow wind warning from 19:00 CET Monday to 04:00 CET Tuesday for western England, Wales, Scotland, and eastern Northern Ireland, warning of more power cuts [19].

Confidence is high on the deaths, the power cuts, and the Dutch freighter, because the BBC and NOS attribute them to police, the Energy Networks Association, the Met Office, and the Dutch coastguard; each country rests on one outlet.

items.title: Italy's Salvini Vows to Press Cabinet to Halt Money and Weapons for Ukraine
items.lede: Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani answered on Monday that a new Italian military aid package for Kyiv is ready and will be sent as soon as possible.

sections.text: Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini was confirmed as secretary of the League (Lega) on Sunday with 465 votes, 76% of the 611 valid ballots, against 146 for challenger Massimo Garavaglia, at the party's extraordinary congress in Milan, La Stampa and ANSA reported [20][21][22]. Three ballots were blank and five invalid, and Salvini will lead the party until 2030 [21][20]. Before the vote, Salvini said that if confirmed he would tell the Council of Ministers to stop money and arms for Ukraine, adding that he would go with this clear position [23]. La Repubblica reported early on Monday that Meloni called Salvini to tell him 'Così mi metti in difficoltà' ('you're putting me in a difficult position') [24]. On Monday Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, asked about Salvini, said a new package of military aid for Kyiv was ready and would be sent as soon as possible, adding that Italy would keep supporting Ukraine for as long as necessary, ANSA reported [25]. No statement from Meloni's office was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the vote and Salvini's statements, because La Stampa and ANSA report them on record; Meloni's call rests on La Repubblica alone, and Tajani's reply rests on an ANSA headline and summary.

items.title: Brussels Police Defend Confiscating Goggles and Saline From Belgian Protesters
items.lede: Officers took swimming and ski goggles and face masks from people heading to Saturday's march, and their commander says the items were seized as a preventive measure.

sections.text: Brussels police said on Sunday that officers acted lawfully when they "preventively" confiscated saline vials, protective, swimming, and ski goggles, and face masks from people about to join Saturday's protest in central Brussels, Belgium, Belga reported [26]. Several hundred people had gathered at the Mont des Arts before the march, at the call of groups including the Front des Mères and École en Lutte [27]. Commissioner Linda Camarero-Verde of the Brussels-Capital-Ixelles police zone acknowledged that carrying such items is not banned but said the march was tolerated only on condition that no irregularities occurred, calling the measures specific to its context [26]. Brussels police said about 400 people took part; five were detained for disturbing public order and four arrested over prohibited weapons and incitement to violence [28][29]. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said on X that the protests ended without major incident, thanked police for their firmness, and said those behind damage and fires must be identified and punished [28]. No complaint or court challenge was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the police statement, because only Belga via La Libre reports it so far; confidence is high on Saturday's arrest figures, because Belga, RTBF, La Libre, and Reuters report them.

items.title: Le Pen Opens French Presidential Bid Promising a Bardella-Led Unity Government
items.lede: The National Rally leader, ahead in every poll for next May's election, also vowed to write the 'national community' into the Constitution and keep young people out of foreign wars.

sections.text: France's far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen launched her presidential campaign on Sunday at the party's congress in Orléans, promising a "national unity" and "pluralist" government led by party president Jordan Bardella if she wins next May, AFP reported [9][30]. "The state we want will not be RN" but a patriotic, non-partisan collective work, she said [9][30]. She said she would write "the national community" into the Constitution and recognise only one people, and pledged that France would not send young people to die in wars "that are not ours" [9]. During Bardella's earlier speech, party stewards removed several people from the hall, including Union of Jewish Students of France activists who unfurled a banner; the group said they were removed very violently [9]. The congress was held under heavy security, with protests banned in the city [9]. No government reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on Le Pen's pledges, because AFP reports them via 20 Minutes and La Libre; the account of the stewards' force rests on the student group's statement.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Russian Officials Detain a Polish Hiker Who Crossed From Lithuania on the Curonian Spit
items.lede: Lithuanian border guards said it was the first such coastal crossing into Russia since 2018 and are weighing a pre-trial investigation into illegal border crossing.

sections.text: A Polish man walking along the Baltic Sea coast on the Curonian Spit is suspected of ignoring warning signs and walking from Lithuania into Russian territory, where he was detained, Lithuania's State Border Guard Service (VSAT) said on Monday [1]. VSAT said Russian officials had confirmed the detention and that it was clarifying details before deciding on a pre-trial investigation [1]. The last recorded crossing from Lithuania into Russia along the coast was in 2018, and one in the opposite direction was in 2017 [1]. The man's name and the date of the crossing were not given, and no Polish or Russian statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on a Lithuanian border-guard statement reported by LRT.

items.title: Latvia's CERT Reports Hundreds of Failed Hacking Attempts on Websites
items.lede: About five public sites, including Latvian Radio's, were still offline after last week's emergency patching, though CERT.lv says no site has been breached.

sections.text: Latvia's cyber incident response center CERT.lv told Latvian Radio there had been hundreds of attempts to hack Latvian websites in recent days, none successful [2]. Last week many government, local authority, and private websites in Latvia and abroad were taken offline because of a security vulnerability and had to be updated urgently [2]. About five websites of public importance remained down, including the state healthcare queue site rindapiearsta.lv, Rīgas siltums, and Latvian Radio, and many others were still unreachable from abroad [2]. Deputy head Varis Teivāns said activity was noticeable but not extraordinary, because exploiting the flaw requires specific knowledge of each target system [2].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on CERT.lv statements to Latvian Radio; the attackers were not identified.

items.title: Lithuania Expands Šiauliai Air Base to Host Up to 750 NATO Troops
items.lede: The Defense Ministry wants the base ready for fifth-generation fighters by the second half of 2028 and puts a 500-troop mission's yearly economic impact near €65.5 million.

sections.text: Lithuania's expansion of its air force base at Šiauliai will let it host 500 to 750 NATO troops on a rotational basis, the Defense Ministry said on Monday [3]. The ministry said a rotation of 200 troops now generates about €24.6 million a year for the economy, against about €65.5 million for a 500-troop mission, with each soldier spending €2,000 to €2,300 a month [3]. It plans to adapt the base for fifth-generation fighter jets by the second half of 2028 [3]. Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said the investment strengthens Lithuania's defense and benefits the economy [3]. No timetable for larger rotations was given.
Confidence is moderate, because the figures are the ministry's own estimates relayed by LRT; no second outlet was checked.

items.title: Estonia's Herem Wants the 10-Year Defense Plan Reopened for Air and Sea Gaps
items.lede: The defense minister said the plan, already awaiting government approval, needs changes because of lessons from Ukraine, including a possible purchase of light jets against drones.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem told ERR that the country's 10-year national defense development plan, which had reached the Government Office for approval, needs improvements in air and maritime defense, including keeping Gulf of Finland shipping lanes open [4]. He said Russia has fielded cheap cruise missiles and jet-powered drones over the past year, and that aircraft are among the most effective means against them, whether light jets such as the Hawk or L-39 or unmanned jets [4]. Herem called a light-jet purchase realistic and possibly necessary, but said the wider air defense picture, available runways in wartime, and the number of aircraft must be reviewed first, and that resources are limited [4]. On 25 October he had told ERR that Estonia could need around a dozen such jets and that procurement could take up to four years [5].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the minister's own interviews with ERR; no government decision on the plan was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Kulbergs Delays Latvia's Coalition Talks, Leaving Partners Without a Program
items.lede: Formal talks on the next government are now due to start on Wednesday, 28 October, with the National Alliance first in line.

sections.text: Nearly all of October has passed in Latvia without formal party consultations on the next government, and neither politicians nor the public have seen Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's promised change plan, coalition model, or ministers, LTV's De facto reported [6]. Kulbergs, whose United List holds 41 seats, postponed the plan's presentation after travelling to a friend's funeral in the United States, and says formal talks will begin on Wednesday [6]. The National Alliance will go first, and many of its members want Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava to keep his post [6]. New Unity also has an invitation and said it would not back golden-visa schemes [6]. Latvia First leader Ainārs Šlesers again offered a United List coalition with 58 votes or support for a minority government without posts [6].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one LTV programme; the timetable and positions are the politicians' own statements to it.

items.title: Latvian Prosecutor Says Belarusian Guards Send Indebted Migrants to Sabotage the Border
items.lede: Latvia has logged more than 60 cases of damaged border infrastructure this year, against 23 in all of 2025, as the Belarus-backed migration route strains.

sections.text: A Latvian prosecutor told LTV's De facto programme that uniformed officials visit migrant camps on the Belarusian side, check whether people have paid for an illegal crossing, and send those who have not to damage Latvia's border infrastructure, with beatings or torture if they refuse [7]. Andris Aleksejevs of the Prosecutor General's Office said a criminal case opened in July rests on reasonable suspicion that Belarusian border guard officials are involved in organising illegal migration and damaging Latvian infrastructure [7]. Border guard data show more than 60 cases of damage this year, including electrical cabinets and cameras, against 23 last year, and more than 12,000 illegal crossing attempts have been prevented in 2026 [7]. Smugglers on the Belarusian side threw stones at border guards at least twice last week, De facto reported [7]. A Telegram group calling itself the Black Russians claimed one sabotage episode in early October [7]. No Belarusian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LTV report quoting Latvian prosecutors, border guards, and the military; the claims about Belarusian officials are allegations in an open criminal case.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Bulgaria's Yotova and Gyurov Head for a 1 November Presidential Run-Off
items.lede: The fully processed commission count gives the Radev-backed incumbent a lead of almost three points, and Radev now frames the run-off as a choice between peace and war.

sections.text: With 99.94 percent of ballots processed, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission had acting President Iliana Yotova on 34.8 percent and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov on 31.9 percent, Balkan Insight reported on Monday [1]. With 100 percent of polling-station protocols processed, the commission had Yotova on 34.76 percent, Gyurov on 31.95 percent, and Revival leader Kostadin Kostadinov third on 12.54 percent, BNT reported [2]. Because no ticket won a majority, the top two meet in a run-off on 1 November [1] [2]. Alpha Research put turnout at a record low of 22.5 percent, against 40.5 percent in 2021, as GERB and Delyan Peevski's DPS-New Beginning fielded no candidates [1]. On Monday Prime Minister Rumen Radev said voters would choose between peace and war, casting Gyurov's pro-EU, pro-Ukraine stance as warmongering, while Gyurov again challenged Yotova to a TV debate she has so far declined [1]. Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev had called polling day calm [3].
Confidence is high on the run-off pairing and the commission figures, which BIRN and BNT agree on; turnout is a pollster's estimate.

items.title: Serbia's Student List Wins a Parliamentary Majority as Vučić Concedes Defeat
items.lede: Official commission figures on Monday gave the movement 52.65 percent on 68.8 percent turnout, and it has yet to name a prime ministerial candidate.

sections.text: Serbia's Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) said on Monday that, with 8,135 of 8,392 polling stations counted, the opposition Student List had won the 25 October snap parliamentary election, in which 18 lists were on the ballot [4], with 52.65 percent, against 39.2 percent for Aleksandar Vučić's United Serbia, on turnout of 68.8 percent [5]. Ipsos and CeSID projections at 96 percent of the sample gave the Student List 52.9 percent and 140 of 250 seats, against 103 for United Serbia, with minority lists sharing the rest [5] [6]; 126 seats are needed for a majority [7]. Vučić conceded on Sunday evening, calling the result the verification of a revolution backed by European countries and the US deep state [8]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU stood ready to support reforms, Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said the door to the EU was open, and Montenegro's prime minister Milojko Spajić hoped for better ties [9]. The movement, born of protests after the 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse, has not named a prime ministerial candidate [5].
Confidence is high: the commission's partial count and the Ipsos and CeSID projections agree closely; final certified results were not found by the cutoff.

items.title: Albania's Rama Unveils Fines of Up to €5,000 for Defying Protest Dispersal Orders
items.lede: Activists say the package threatens free assembly, after police arrested 23 people over Saturday's clashes and detained more protesters outside Rama's office on Sunday.

sections.text: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday announced a package against "violence and urban anarchy" after weeks of clashes in Tirana, blaming opposition leader Sali Berisha, "Antifa extremists", and foreign actors, Balkan Insight reported on Monday [10]. It would fine participants in unauthorized gatherings €100 to €1,000, and up to €5,000 for ignoring dispersal orders or hiding identity, let police limit protests at some public institutions, and make organizing a banned gathering a criminal offense [10]. It also bars teachers from taking under-18s to gatherings and creates an electronic register of suspects [10]. On Sunday evening, the 13th day of protests, police took some protesters into custody outside Rama's office [11]. State Police said they had arrested 23 people and declared 30 wanted after Saturday's protest [12], when tear gas, water cannon, and rubber bullets were used [10]. The Health Ministry had put injuries since the protests began on 13 October at 310, including 191 police officers, in an update at 21:00 on 19 October (20:00 CET) [13].
Confidence is moderate: the law's terms are Rama's own announcement relayed by BIRN, and the arrest figures are police statements; no Monday protest tally was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Georgia's Prison Service Chief Pataridze Quits Amid an Inmate-Beating Probe
items.lede: He went hours after the Prosecutor General's Office urged his suspension over injuries to detainee Davit Peikrishvili, and a former regional police chief reportedly replaces him.

sections.text: Giorgi Pataridze, head of Georgia's Special Penitentiary Service, resigned on 26 October after the Prosecutor General's Office recommended that the Justice Ministry suspend him, the service confirmed to Interpressnews, Civil Georgia reported [1]. Prosecutors told OC Media the case of inmate Davit Peikrishvili, hospitalized twice with injuries he says came from cellmates, had moved from the ministry's inspectorate to their investigators [2]. Peikrishvili's lawyer alleges rivals Vato Kipiani and Avtandil Bilanishvili were deliberately placed in his cell; Kipiani denies it [1] [2]. The prison service had denied any assault [2]. Civil Georgia said Ramaz Tatarashvili, former Shida Kartli police chief, reportedly replaces him, and that Pataridze's predecessor also quit over an inmate-beating probe in 2025 [1].
Confidence is high on the resignation and the prosecutors' recommendation, which two outlets report from official statements; the assault claims are disputed.

items.title: Armenia's Ruling Civil Contract Loses Only Stepanavan in 21 Local Races
items.lede: Official commission figures for 19 communities show Pashinyan's party beaten only where a Strong Armenia candidate was jailed on vote-buying charges before polling day.

sections.text: Armenia's Central Electoral Commission had published results for 19 of the 21 communities that voted on 25 October by Monday afternoon, and Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract lost only Stepanavan, OC Media reported [3]. There the Entrepreneur Party took 41.54 percent against 35.32 percent for Civil Contract [3]. The opposition contested 14 communities, and Civil Contract ran unopposed in some [3]. On 21 October the Investigative Committee announced 14 arrests in Stepanavan, including Strong Armenia's candidate Arsen Gevorgyan, on electoral bribery charges [3] [4]. Preliminary figures relayed on Sunday night by Caucasian Knot had shown Civil Contract with up to 96 percent in Vayk and the Solidarity alliance ahead in Goris and Gavar [4], which the commission results reported by OC Media do not bear out [3]. Observers reported breaches of ballot secrecy [4].
Confidence is moderate: OC Media cites published commission results, but they conflict with earlier preliminary figures for Goris and Gavar, and two communities were still undeclared.

items.title: Georgia's Opposition Launches a 'Georgia Without Ivanishvili' Protest Wave
items.lede: Thousands marched as the court hearing on Georgian Dream's bid to ban opposition parties resumed on Monday, with the next big rally set for 28 November.

sections.text: Opposition parties and civil society groups in Georgia marched from Tbilisi State University toward Rustaveli Avenue on 25 October under the slogan "Georgia without Ivanishvili", which organisers called the start of a new wave of protests, Caucasian Knot reported [5]. Citing Publika video, it said thousands took part, carrying Georgian, Ukrainian, and EU flags, with a large police presence [5]. The march came as the Constitutional Court considers Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban opposition parties [5]. Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia said the movement needed a culmination on 28 November, two years after protests began [5] [6]. European Georgia leader Gigi Tsereteli said parties were being banned and political life restricted [6]. Genews reported that the rally ended at about 22:37 local time (19:37 CET) [6]. The previous evening's weekly march drew hundreds [7]. Civil Georgia said the nine-party Opposition Alliance organized the march on the anniversary of the disputed 2024 election, and that the ban lawsuit now also targets For Georgia, the only opposition party in Parliament [8]. No detentions were reported for Sunday's march by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: three outlets agree on the march and the speeches, but the crowd size rests on Publika video cited by Caucasian Knot, and no police figure was found.

items.title: Stuttgart Police Brace for Saturday's Nationwide Gen Z Protests in Germany
items.lede: Police say they see no concrete sign of French-style violence locally, but promise to intervene against any disorder at the 14:00 Schlossplatz rally.

sections.text: The initiative 'Gen Z regelt' plans demonstrations on Saturday, 31 October, in 23 German cities, including Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Freiburg, and Ulm in Baden-Württemberg [1] [2]. In Stuttgart, participants are to gather on the Schlossplatz at 14:00 before a march through the city center; Karlsruhe starts at 16:00 [1]. Stuttgart police said on Monday that they are monitoring mobilization on social networks and the security situation, citing violent youth protests elsewhere in Europe, especially France, but have no concrete indications of similar incidents in Stuttgart [1]. Police President Markus Eisenbraun said peaceful protest would be protected, while disruption, property damage, or attacks on people would be met by police action [2]. The organizers protest rising living costs, cuts in education, and military conscription [2] [1]. More than 9,400 people had signed up on the initiative's website for the Stuttgart demonstration by 24 October, a local news portal reported [1].

Confidence is high on the protest dates, cities, and the police statement, because the Stuttgarter Zeitung and dpa via TAG24 report them. Confidence is low on the expected turnout, which rests on online sign-ups relayed from one local portal.

items.title: German Business Sentiment Rises for a Sixth Month to Highest Since Early 2023
items.lede: Manufacturers drove the gain as new orders rose, despite high energy prices and unrest in neighboring countries, though one bank analyst saw no investment upswing.

sections.text: Germany's ifo business climate index rose to 90.2 points in October from 89.9 in September, the Munich institute said on Monday, driven by more confident expectations while firms rated current business slightly worse [3]. It was the sixth rise in a row and the highest level since spring 2023; analysts had expected 89.9 [4]. In manufacturing, both the current situation and expectations turned positive for the first time in more than three years as new orders rose, and firms plan to raise output [3]. Sentiment in services weakened, except among IT providers, while trade was unchanged and construction improved [3]. ifo President Clemens Fuest said the recovery continues [4]. IKB analyst Klaus Bauknecht said the survey gave no sign of a sustained investment upswing [4].
Confidence is high on the index figures, which come from the ifo press release and are reported by tagesschau. Analysts' views are their own readings of the survey.

items.title: Merz Leaves for Singapore, Japan, and South Korea as Steinmeier Visits China
items.lede: The parallel tours split the work: the chancellor courts partners to cut reliance on Beijing, while the president presses Xi on trade fairness and Russia's war.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz began a five-day trip to Singapore, Japan, and South Korea on Monday with about 30 senior business representatives from industry, technology, defense, and energy [5] [6]. Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier began a separate state visit to China the same day [7] [5]. Merz told the Bundestag in mid-October that the three countries are central to reducing critical one-sided dependencies, meaning above all on China [6]. He is to meet Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and South Korea's President Lee Jae-myung, and open the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul [5]. Arms cooperation is on the agenda at every stop [7]. Steinmeier plans a speech at Peking University on Thursday and talks with Xi Jinping on Friday, and wants to urge China to use its influence on Russia to end the attacks on Ukraine [7] [6].

Confidence is high on the itineraries, delegation, and stated aims, because tagesschau, DW, and Deutschlandfunk report them from government and presidential office statements. No departure time was published in the sources read.

items.title: Storm Gust Drives a Cruise Ship Into Freighters in Germany's Bremerhaven
items.lede: No one was hurt, but crushed lifeboats kept the 2,428-guest Mein Schiff 3 in port as forecasters expected a storm surge in Hamburg overnight.

sections.text: Storm Luise seriously injured two people in Nastätten, Rhineland-Palatinate, on Friday [8] [9]. On Sunday, storm Manja brought gale warnings to much of Germany, with 135 km/h measured on the Brocken [10]; in Freiburg, a gust cut power for some 25,000 people until midday [11]. In Bremerhaven, TUI Cruises' Mein Schiff 3 collided while leaving port on Sunday evening; police later said three ships were involved [12]. A heavy gust pushed the ship against the freighter MSC Victorine around 17:00, crushing lifeboats and tenders, and authorities barred the onward voyage to the Canary Islands [13]. The container ship has a 10-metre tear but no water ingress; 2,428 guests and 922 crew were aboard, and the water police are investigating the cause [12]. The federal maritime agency had forecast a storm surge for the night into Monday, with high water 1.5 to 2 metres above mean high water on the East Frisian coast and in the Elbe area [10]; on Monday it issued a fresh storm-surge warning valid until the afternoon, and no ferries ran to the Halligen, NDR reported [14].

Confidence is high on the collision and damage, which tagesschau and Merkur attribute to police, port authorities, and TUI Cruises, and moderate on the gust as cause and on surge levels, which rest on forecasts.

items.title: Germany's Audi Chief Faces Union Fury Over Trump Rally Plant Announcement
items.lede: Labor leaders on VW's supervisory board say they will not approve the Georgia factory without clarity on German plants, leaving the 4-billion-dollar project open.

sections.text: German carmaker Audi, a Volkswagen subsidiary, said it plans its first U.S. production site in Georgia, investing around $4 billion and creating about 4,500 jobs [15]. President Donald Trump announced the project at a Republican campaign event in Georgia on Saturday, with Audi chief Gernot Döllner joining him on stage [16]. On Monday, VW works council head Daniela Cavallo said in an internal interview that Döllner had given active campaign help and that VW's board had let itself become a puppet in Trump's propaganda show [17] [18]. IG Metall chief Christiane Benner, VW's deputy supervisory board chair, called the appearance politically unacceptable and a breach of Audi's rule barring public events with candidates in the three months before elections [17] [18]. A German government spokesperson declined to comment, calling it a business decision [18]. Cavallo said labor representatives would not approve a new US plant without a full picture of the impact on German sites, so the decision is still open [17]; the VW supervisory board has the final say [19] [20].

Confidence is high on the quotes and the plant plan, because tagesschau, citing dpa, and The Guardian report them, and Audi's release states the figures. Confidence is moderate on any breach of company rules, which rests on labor leaders' reading of Audi's guidelines.

items.title: Two SPD Ministers Unveil a Bill Letting Builders Skip Costly Comfort Standards
items.lede: Germany's ministries expect simpler homes to cut building costs by 10 to 15 percent, though the CDU wanted no separate contract type.

sections.text: German Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig and Construction Minister Verena Hubertz (both SPD) present a draft 'Gebäudetyp E' law on Monday that would let parties to a building contract agree to waive non-mandatory comfort standards [21] [22]. Examples include thinner ceilings, fewer sockets, lower ceiling heights, and unheated stairwells; fire safety, structural safety, ventilation, and light are excluded [21]. Ministries expect building costs to fall by 10 to 15 percent, citing pilot projects [21]. The draft, seen by ARD, makes the option a separate voluntary contract category, a point CDU housing spokesman Jan-Marco Luczak had opposed, arguing it could create two-class building [22]. The bill now goes to the federal states and industry associations for comment, and is not yet agreed within the government [22] [21]. The ministers aim for it to take effect in mid-2027 at the earliest [21].

Confidence is high on the draft's content and timing, because ARD has seen it and dpa reports the ministers' own statements. Confidence is moderate on the savings estimate, which rests on the ministries' reading of pilot projects.

items.title: Germany's Söder Presses for a November Deal on Aigner as Merz Stays Silent
items.lede: The CDU will not take up the presidency question until 9 November, deputy leader Michael Kretschmer said, while an SPD state leader called Aigner very suitable.

sections.text: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) closed the CSU party congress in Munich, Germany, on Saturday but said nothing about the CSU's push for Bavarian Landtag President Ilse Aigner as federal president, though mentioning her at the start of his speech set off a storm of cheering among delegates, most of whom rose from their seats [23] [24]. CDU women want one of their own, and the CDU claims the nomination [25] [26]. Merz said anyone thinking of voting AfD 'has no place in our Union' [24]. On Sunday SPD chief whip Dirk Wiese and Greens parliamentary leader Britta Haßelmann said the office should go to a woman [27]. On ARD on Sunday evening, Söder said a decision would best come 'now in November' and that the CSU had held neither the chancellery nor the presidency in 75 years [28] [25]. Saxony's premier and CDU deputy leader Michael Kretschmer called Aigner excellent but not the only suitable candidate, saying the CDU would discuss it on 9 November [28]. Bremen's SPD mayor Andreas Bovenschulte called her very suitable, saying the CDU and Merz must now decide [28].
Confidence is high on the quoted remarks, reported by tagesschau, dpa, and n-tv, and moderate on the CDU position, which rests partly on unnamed party circles.
